extracted.intended_audience: users and developers of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, computational algebraists, and programmers using Singular/Plural)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the Singular programming language and its Plural (non-commutative) extension: commands, system variables, limitations, language differences, and data-type conventions. Intended to guide correct use and avoid common pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library and dynamic-module loading behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time a library or dynamic module is loaded the corresponding package is created (package name derived from file name for libraries; hard-coded for dynamic modules). Only the names of procedures in the library are loaded; the body of a procedure is read during its first call. Starting Singular with -q/--quiet suppresses library-loading messages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use option(loadLib) to show loading of libraries (example: load("inout.lib"); then listvar() shows procedure names). This minimizes memory consumption by unused procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: quit / exit command
rubrics_metrics.description: quit (or exit) terminates Singular; works inside a procedure or from an interrupt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: quit; Example: quit; (same as exit;).

rubrics_metrics.name: return statement syntax and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: return ( expression list ); or return(); returns procedure result(s) and can only be used inside a procedure. Brackets are required even if no return value is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: return(j); return(); return (1,2); return types may vary with input; if return type varies, assign to a def variable to capture it.

rubrics_metrics.name: while loop behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: while (boolean expression) block. The boolean expression is evaluated and if TRUE the block executes repeatedly until the boolean is FALSE. The break command leaves the innermost while.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows both finite and infinite loops and use of break to exit. See Section 5.2 for related control constructs.

rubrics_metrics.name: break point (~;)
rubrics_metrics.description: ~; sets a break point: when Singular reaches ~; it prompts for input and activates debug mode. Execution proceeds after an empty input line; line length <= 80 characters while at breakpoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for inspecting local variables while debugging procedures. See Section 3.9.3/3.9.4 for debugger details.

rubrics_metrics.name: degBound system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: degBound (int): the standard-basis computation is stopped if the total (weighted) degree exceeds degBound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reset with degBound = 0 (infinite). Do not use degBound for a global ordering with inhomogeneous input unless ordering is dp or Dp. Exact meaning of 'degree' depends on ring ordering and command: slimgb uses total degree with weights 1; std uses it for block orderings only.

rubrics_metrics.name: echo system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: echo (int): input is echoed if echo >= voice. echo is a procedure-local setting defaulted to 0 and does not affect command output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: echo = 1; int i = echo; Use with voice and dbprint to control displayed comments during procedure execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: minpoly system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: minpoly (number): describes the coefficient field of the current basering as an algebraic extension with minimal polynomial equal to minpoly. The minpoly must be specified after defining the ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The polynomial's variable is the algebraic element (not a ring variable). Singular does not check irreducibility — use factorize to check. Example: ring Cxyz=(0,i),(x,y,z),dp; minpoly=i^2+1;

rubrics_metrics.name: multBound system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: multBound (int): the standard-basis computation is stopped if the ideal is zero-dimensional in a ring with local ordering and its multiplicity is lower than multBound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reset by multBound = 0 to disable. Example demonstrates multBound affecting std results and degree (multiplicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: noether system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: noether (poly): in local rings, the standard-basis computation cuts off all monomials strictly larger (w.r.t. monomial ordering) than the monomial noether during the computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reset with noether = 0 to disable. Example shows how setting noether can simplify std output.

rubrics_metrics.name: printlevel system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: printlevel (int): sets the debug level for dbprint. If printlevel >= voice then dbprint acts like print; otherwise dbprint prints nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use with voice to control debug-comment display while procedures execute. Example toggles printlevel to show dbprint output.

rubrics_metrics.name: short system variable (monomial output format)
rubrics_metrics.description: short (int): controls monomial output formatting. If short != 0 the short C-like notation is used; if short == 0 a C-like notation with explicit * is used. The default depends on ring variable names and is ring-local.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example toggles short between 1 and 0 showing '2x2 x2' vs '2*x^2 x^2'. Changing basering restores previous value for that ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: timer system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: timer (int): if timer > 0 the CPU time used for each command is printed (if > minimal time and printlevel+1 >= voice). Also yields CPU time since start-up in a configurable resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defaults: timer=0, minimal time=0.5s, resolution unit=1s. Options --min-time and --ticks-per-sec adjust behavior. On Windows95/98 timer is unreliable — use rtimer instead. Examples show measuring elapsed time sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRACE system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: TRACE (int): sets debugging verbosity (bit/level-coded). TRACE=0 no debugging messages; TRACE=1 messages about entering/leaving procedures; TRACE=3 includes line numbers; TRACE=4 echoes each line and suspends interpretation until RETURN; higher bits can show kernel calls, assigns, automatic conversions, profiling, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRACE defaults to 0 and does not affect command output. Useful to trace nested procedure calls; examples show entering/leaving messages at multiple levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: rtimer system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: rtimer (int): like timer, but reports real (wall-clock) times. Reliable on all operating systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when wall-clock timing is required or when timer is unreliable on an OS.

rubrics_metrics.name: voice system variable
rubrics_metrics.description: voice (int): shows the nesting level of procedures; used to control the display of comments while procedures execute (used together with dbprint/printlevel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows voice incrementing inside a procedure call. Use voice to compare with printlevel for debug output control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime-field characteristic limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The characteristic of a prime field must be less than or equal to 2147483647 (2^31). Factory routines and certain libraries impose stricter bounds (e.g., 2^29 or 2^30 limits in contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of lower bounds in factory and NTL routines when choosing prime characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite field size limit (GF(p,n))
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of elements in GF(p,n) must be less than 65536.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose extension degrees accordingly; this is a hard system limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial (weighted) degree limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The (weighted) degree of a monomial must be <= 2147483647.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit is dependent on ring ordering and affects computations that measure degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank limit for free modules
rubrics_metrics.description: The rank of any free module must be <= 2147483647.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-rank modules may hit system limits; design computations accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal exponent of ring variable
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximal allowed exponent of a ring variable depends on the ordering of the ring and is at least 32767.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See monomial ordering settings (Section B.2) to change limits if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precision limit for long floating point numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The precision of long floating point numbers (for ground field real) must be <= 32767.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure requested precision does not exceed this bound when using real ground fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integer (int) range
rubrics_metrics.description: Integers of type int are limited to the range -2147483648 to 2147483647.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bigint if larger integers are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Floating-point range and input syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating point numbers (type number from field real) have machine-dependent ranges (typical -1.0e-38 to 1.0e+38). String representation of overflow/underflow is machine-dependent. Input syntax is given by scanf but must start with a digit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious about platform differences; ensure numeric literals start with a digit.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMP-based floating precision internal setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Floating point numbers with precision p use internally mpf_set_default_prec(3.5*p+1). Their input syntax is given by mpf_set_str and must start with a digit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects internal precision allocation when using GMP-backed reals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier display truncation
rubrics_metrics.description: The length of an identifier is unlimited but listvar displays only the first 20 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of display truncation when inspecting long identifiers; the identifier itself can be longer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement token count limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements may not contain more than 10000 tokens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long statements should be broken up to avoid exceeding token limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Tokens (strings, numbers, ...) may not be longer than 16382 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long tokens (e.g., huge numeric literals or strings) will violate this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Input must be 7-bit clean
rubrics_metrics.description: All input to Singular must be 7-bit clean: special characters (e.g., German Umlauts, French accents) may not appear in input, libraries, or procedure definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASCII-only input or appropriate encoding conversion before feeding input to Singular.

rubrics_metrics.name: System-dependent dynamic module availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Dynamic modules are implemented only for Unix systems with ELF executables (Linux, Solaris, FreeBSD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On other platforms dynamic modules may be unavailable or limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No rvalue for increments and assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: The increment (++) / decrement (--) operators have no rvalue — they cannot be used in expressions to produce values. Assignment expressions do not have results; compound chained assignments like i = j = k; are not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate statements: i++; j = i; Avoid writing j = i++; which gives an error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical expressions are fully evaluated (no short-circuit)
rubrics_metrics.description: All arguments of a logical expression are evaluated before determining the overall value. There is no left-to-right short-circuiting, so constructs like (defined(i) && i>0) can error if i is undefined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workarounds: (1) Use defined(i) alone as boolean flag; (2) define variables before first use (e.g., if (!defined(DEBUG)) { int DEBUG = 1; }). Use nested ifs instead of relying on short-circuit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No case/switch statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular lacks a case/switch construct; emulate it with a while(1) loop and sequential ifs each ending with break.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pattern provided in documentation demonstrates how to implement a multi-branch dispatch with breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma usage differs from C
rubrics_metrics.description: A comma separates list elements and the comma expression evaluates to a list; commas cannot combine several expressions into one as in C. Example: for (i=1, j=5; ...) is WRONG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the language's for-loop initializers correctly: for (i,j = 1,5; ...). Use div for integer division and be careful with whitespace in numeric division.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brackets and block syntax requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Curly braces { } must always enclose the statement body following constructs like if, else, for, while, even if the block has a single statement. Similarly, return must have parentheses even if no value: return();
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if (i == 1) return i; is WRONG — must be if (i == 1) { return (i); }.

rubrics_metrics.name: continue behavior inside loops
rubrics_metrics.description: continue is valid only inside for or while and skips the rest of the loop body jumping to the beginning of the block; unlike C, it does not execute the loop's increment statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates setting the loop variable inside the body before continue to alter next iteration value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure return types and assignment to def
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures are strongly typed but need not declare a return type; the return value may vary with input. If a procedure returns varying types, assign its return value to a variable of type def. If a procedure changes the current ring and returns a ring-dependent value, the caller must assign to def.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proc type_return(int i) { if (i>0) return(i); else return(list(i)); } then def t1 = type_return(1); typeof(t1) == int; def t2 = type_return(-1); typeof(t2) == list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing starts at 1
rubrics_metrics.description: All indexed objects (vectors, modules, polynomials, ideals, intvec, etc.) use 1-based indexing; the first index is 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: vector h=[x+y,x,z]; h[1] -> x+y; p[2] for poly p=x+y+z -> y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integer division whitespace quirk
rubrics_metrics.description: Division of numeric constants depends on surrounding whitespace: '3/2' (no spaces) treats constants as type number and uses ring division; '3 / 2' (spaces) treats them as ints and uses integer division. This quirk affects large numeric constants too.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use div for integer division (3 div 2) and explicit casts number(3)/number(2) for ring division to avoid ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomial formation precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Monomial formation has precedence over all operators: a coefficient optionally followed by a sequence of ring variables (with optional exponents) without whitespace forms a monomial. This affects parsing: e.g., 2xy^2 is grouped differently than 2x*y^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit with * and parentheses when needed; in non-commutative contexts use '*' to indicate multiplication order explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of mult(i) depends on monomial ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ideal or module i, mult(i) returns the multiplicity of the ideal generated by the leading monomials of the given generators, hence it depends on the monomial ordering. For dp ordering and when i is a standard basis, mult(i) corresponds to the degree of the homogeneous ideal from homogenization and setting the homogenizing variable to 0 (degree of the part at infinity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret mult(i) or degree(i) for inhomogeneous ideals as the degree of the homogenization's affine part unless you understand the ordering semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: size vs ncols for ideals/modules
rubrics_metrics.description: size counts the non-zero entries (non-zero generators) of an ideal or module; ncols returns the actual number of entries (columns) including zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ncols to determine the declared number of generators; use size for count of non-zero generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computations in qring (quotient rings)
rubrics_metrics.description: To speed up computations in quotient rings, Singular usually does not reduce polynomials with respect to the quotient ideal, instead it uses given representatives as long as possible. Reduction is performed when necessary, e.g., during standard-basis computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If manual reduction is needed, use reduce(f,std(0)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree semantics vary by command
rubrics_metrics.description: The meaning of 'degree' depends on the command: slimgb uses total degree with weights 1; std uses total degree only for block orderings; hilb uses total degree with weights 1 (unless weight vector provided); kbase uses total degree with weights 1 unless weightKB is set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware which 'degree' notion a command uses before interpreting results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substring selection semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: String substring selection differs depending on bracket contents: s[2,6] (two ints) returns a substring where first int = start position and second int = length (returns a string). s[intvec(2,6)] returns characters at the specified positions and yields an expression list of strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain a string of selected characters, assign s[intvec(...)] to a string variable (stick together by assignment). Examples illustrate differences and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packages and indexed variables visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables indexed with parentheses in a package are stored in that package and not in Toplevel. listvar() and listvar(package) show different visibility. Example demonstrates package K storing indexed variables that do not appear at toplevel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use package-qualified declarations to manage visibility and avoid name conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifier resolution order and naming recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: An identifier is resolved in the following order: (1) reserved name, (2) local variable (procedure), (3) local ring variable (procedure-local basering), (4) global variable, (5) global ring variable, (6) monomial consisting of local ring variables (no operators), (7) monomial consisting of global ring variables. This allows general variables with same names as ring variables but can produce surprising results when names conflict or when one variable name is a substring of another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strongly recommend not using variables with the same names as ring variables and avoid ring variable names that are substrings of other ring variables. Examples demonstrate surprising resolutions like '2x1' vs '2*x1'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural: scope and main purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural is a kernel extension of Singular providing algorithms for computations within certain non-commutative algebras (G-algebras with PBW bases). It uses the same data structures and allows transferring objects between commutative Singular rings and non-commutative rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Plural to set up G-algebras (see nc_algebra and nc algebra setup functions) and perform computations on polynomials, ideals, vectors, and modules in non-commutative settings. See Section 7.3 for available functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural limitations (what Plural does not do)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural does not perform computations in the free algebra or general factor algebras (except via LETTERPLACE); it requires a monomial ordering and currently supports only global orderings (except SCA which allows a tensor product with a commutative algebra); Plural does not handle non-commutative parameters (parameters cannot be non-commuting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design workflows accordingly: if you need free-algebra computations or non-commutative parameters, consider other approaches or future enhancements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural conventions: notation and default meanings
rubrics_metrics.description: In Plural, multiplication in non-commutative case must be written with '*', e.g., y*x; plain 'yx' or 'xy' are interpreted as commutative expressions. Plural output omits '*' signs (consists only of monomials). By default, an 'ideal' in Plural means a list of generators of a left ideal; modules are finitely generated left submodules or factor modules by left submodules; qring (plural) only supports factor-algebras modulo two-sided ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To compute two-sided Groebner bases use twostd. Be explicit about multiplication and ideal/module sidedness to avoid semantic mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal (plural): left-ideal representation and declaration syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: In Plural, ideals are left ideals represented as lists of polynomials interpreted as left generators. Declaration syntax: ideal name = list of poly and ideal expressions ; or ideal name = ideal expression ; Default value: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: size counts non-zero generators, ncols counts all generators. Examples show ideal creation with zeros and simplification behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal expressions (plural): allowed forms
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal expression may be (1) an identifier of type ideal, (2) a function returning an ideal, (3) a combination of ideal expressions using + or *, (4) a power of an ideal expression (^ or **), (5) a type cast to ideal. Product i*i uses all products of generators; i^2 uses only different ones and is faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate large ncols for products and powers and show how to construct ideals from vectors using ideal(v).

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal operations and indexing (plural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: + (concatenation and simplification), * (multiplication with simplification when appropriate), ^ (exponentiation by non-negative integer). Indexing: ideal expression [ intvec expression ] indexes polynomial generators; index 1 gives first generator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use simplify to reduce generated lists. Examples show multiplication with vector, ideal powering, and use of II = I[2..4] slicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal-related functions (plural): available API
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural provides a set of ideal/module-related functions: dim (GK-dimension), eliminate, intersect, kbase, lead, lift, liftstd, maxideal, modulo, mres, ncols, nres, oppose, preimage, quotient, reduce, simplify, size, slimgb, std, subst, syz, twostd, vdim, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function's semantics are referenced (e.g., reduce = left normal form w.r.t left Groebner basis; twostd = two-sided Groebner basis computation). See corresponding Section 7.3.xx for detailed usage examples and parameters.
